name: Website SEO Analysis
description: A reviewed report with a list of pages checked, evidence for each finding, and recommended fixes in priority order. It explains missing data and coverage limits without changing the website.
audience: Website owners, SEO teams, and agencies diagnosing search visibility and measurement quality
problem: SEO audits become generic checklists or unsupported scores when the analyst does not map the actual site, reconcile public pages with first-party measurement, and distinguish measured facts from observations and inference.
outcome: A reviewed report with a list of pages checked, evidence for each finding, and recommended fixes in priority order. It explains missing data and coverage limits without changing the website.
whyAi: AI can traverse representative templates, reconcile public, first-party, and third-party evidence, and synthesize a practical agency-style roadmap while keeping claims traceable.
operatorPath: Example request: “Use Website SEO Analysis on [website URL]. Focus on our service pages and guides for UK small businesses. Check navigation, page content and indexing signals. Return findings with evidence, priorities and ways to verify a fix.”
Name the business goal, important sections, target markets and anything outside the review. Add a reporting period if you want search or analytics data included.
Connect available tools or supply approved exports. The agent can start from the public site and record the missing data. Review the findings before assigning fixes.
agentPath: Confirm the website, business goal, sections to inspect and reporting period. Choose representative pages and record what is outside the review.
Inspect pages, navigation, links, metadata, robots rules and sitemaps. Add connected search or analytics data when available; otherwise work from the public site and record the gaps.
Have the findings independently reviewed, resolve unsupported claims, and prioritize fixes by likely value, confidence and effort. Include dependencies and a way to check each fix.
Save the report, list of inspected pages and supporting evidence so someone can check the conclusions and assign follow-up work.
progressSignals: Public site map and representative templates inspected
recovery: If optional providers are unavailable, continue from public pages and record the missing evidence in the source ledger.
If part of the site is inaccessible, narrow the observed scope and label the limitation instead of claiming a complete crawl.
If the target itself cannot be reached or validated, stop with the exact access failure and evidence collected so far.
safeStoppingPoints: Stop after the analysis package; fixes, publishing, tag changes, and indexing requests require separately authorized work.

handoffs.when: A reviewed technical SEO finding should become repository delivery work.
A reviewed page-level content finding should become a bounded refresh.

prerequisites: A reachable website URL and the business problem you want the analysis to help with
If relevant, priority pages or sections, target markets and anything the agent must leave outside the review
Optional Search Console, analytics or research access, approved exports and a reporting period; public pages can support a useful analysis when those sources are unavailable
proof: A list of inspected URLs and evidence sources, with inaccessible pages, missing data and sampling limits kept visible.
Each finding names the affected page, observed evidence, likely consequence, priority, proposed fix and a way to check the result.

Illustrative finding: a service index links to an old URL that returns 404. A current page covers the same service. Record both URLs and give the repair higher priority if that link is an important route to the service.

Proposed fix in that example: point the link to the current canonical URL. Verification: fetch the updated index, follow its link, and check that the destination returns 200 with the expected canonical.
An independently reviewed report and prioritized work list. The analysis ends there; changing the website is a separately authorized job.
whenToUse: A user asks to audit, map, analyze, or diagnose a website's SEO.
A website needs an agency-style technical, on-page, content, measurement, and optional authority/competitive review.
Connected Search Console, Analytics, Tag Manager, or research tools should enrich a public-site analysis.
